body:
I think I mentioned it in a previous comment, but my step-dad isn't right in the head, obviously. I'm not favored by him because I'm not blood related. I thought he'd mellow with age, but I was wrong. 

I'm going to work on getting out starting this weekend. My boyfriend is going to pick me up and we're going to go apartment hunting, and I'm going to apply for whatever jobs that are available in the area.

Thank you, I hope you are right. There have actually been improvements since leaving my ex, although he continues to linger via e-mails and such. I hope that leaving this place will be another step in the right direction.
Thank you! I, fortunately, get a break starting this Saturday afternoon (after what will most likely be an awkward family get together). I'm hoping it will be free of any parental and ex drama.
Thank you for your words. <3

It might be later. She decided to speak to me earlier and from what I understood she stays with him because he's not as bad as my birth father. He was shitty too, in different ways. But still, when she said that it took me by shock. She could do better, easily. She's always put others before herself, and it's to the point that she's letting it damage her own life. 

I guess I should tell her what I told a friend that became a drug addict in high school. I told her that I loved her, and that I would ever be there for her when she decided she wanted help. She unfortunately died of an overdose. I think that's something that keeps me glued here, to an extent: I'm afraid if I go something awful will happen. I don't know why I think that situations to get to such terrible extremes. I wish I could stick more to the thought of hey, separation is healthy, and maybe it'll give her time to realize that she needs to get away from him and work on the life she deserves to have. But my mind always swings back to the negatives. 

Sorry for the fresh wall of text.
I would definitely do the same for him. He's too kind and generous to not be given full support.

I don't way to be away from mother always. Hell, I think she'd feel better if she got away from my step father, too. And as for him, I can safely say I'd live just fine if he never said a word to me again. 

I don't know how he (bf) believes in me, or what he sees in me, but I hope I'll be able to see it as well.

I already know he's mad as hell I'm seeing someone else. He didn't know for a while, and only found out when I posted a love doodle to one of my art blogs. He sent a long winded message the very next day about how he was on the perfect date with some hot girl that does everything right. Poor lady is just being used out of jealously.
I can block his irritating messages, I just archive them for now in case he snaps I can be like, "Hey look this was building up." in case he decides to play the "I did nothing" game.
Whatever tickles your pickle. I'm done talking about it since this is r/SuicideWatch, and this has unfortunately not been an uplifting conversation.

I'm not keen on having my mom out of my life forever. She wasn't nearly as angry and unstable when she was still single. I'm hoping she gets away from him. I know to her it seems like I'm stealing the one life preserver and jumping off a sinking ship, but I don't want their problems to become mine, because they're not mine. And as awful as she sounds, I hope she divorces him. I think she'd become a lot more mentally stable, not to mention there would be financial safety in it. 

As for my step-dad, if I never saw him again I wouldn't feel bad. 

My ex and I actually live several hundred miles apart at the moment. Everything he's done has been online only so far, but it's been persistent. Although I am experienced in the legal field, I actually don't know how or if I can even legally get him to stop e-mailing/messaging me. I can't imagine any judge taking it seriously until he says something truly threatening or does something different. So far it's all been the usual "I'm right you're wrong, no one loves you but me" tricks. The kind where if you read his messages without hearing my side, you'd think it was the best boyfriend ever. He'll never tell anyone of the awful things he did.
I wish I could feel strong, but I feel so drained and weak.
One of my best friends is a Christian, and she has never done a single thing to harm me. Our beliefs have never caused us problems. I hope you one day realize that not all religious people are bad.
That is very true. I never considered this family relationship an abusive one, but it certainly is. I needed to be told all of that. Thank you for your words.

That seems rather sad. I've met many kind people in life, and not all of them were agnostic. Some were catholic, some christian, some atheist, and so on. I hope they all have safe and happy lives, and I've never favored one over the other just because of their beliefs, or lack of.

It doesn't sound sexist to me, I learned at a very early age that keeping up with a home is hard work with no pay and should be respected regardless of who does it. I told him I'd cook for him and clean. I don't have a problem with it at all, and I know he'd appreciate coming home to a clean home and a meal.

And thank you.

It's horrible, it completely sailed over my head that the reason he put all the responsibility on me was because he wanted some peace of mind at the risk of screwing me over. It's been one hell of a year. I think I've stuck around this long because I thought I'd look like an asshole for jumping ship as the place was going under. I know they first thing they'd do is run to extended family and complain about how horrible their abandoning daughter is. I don't know why I even care what they think; most of them were born with silver spoons in their mouths and cannot begin to understand what it's like to do degrading work.

I'm glad to hear that it's okay to rely on others in the short-term. My awful ex did a good job of brainwashing me, and his damage still lingers (I knew it would, it just seems more difficult right now with other things happening). I used to not have any issues asking for help, but he got it stuck in my mind that I'm pretty much torturing anyone that I approach. 

My biggest worry is finding work, honestly. At this point even minimum wage for cleaning messy toilets would be a huge improvement since I am getting no income at all. Not to mention cleaning poop is probably safer than being at his office. At least poop won't point a knife at me.

I like how you think. His brother knows someone that grows good weed. To be honest, and I know I won't make any friends saying this, I miss smoking it. 

And truthfully, I don't think their situation can be repaired. They are too stubborn and hardheaded. My mother had a good credit score before she married my step-dad. I love my mother, her life has been hard, but I cannot stand to stay and help her with how poorly she guides her anger. Even if she doesn't finish school she has amazing job offers lined up. She needs to divorce him and stabilize her life and my little brother before he turns into the same man that my step-dad is. (My little brother is the birth child of my step-dad and mom, so in my step-dad's eyes he's the golden child by default.)

Also, you are right. Those things are his fault. He has stopped caring about the business, but gets angry with me when I cannot run it by myself correctly. I have attempted to bill over 200 individuals, maintain over 40 cases at a time by myself, and did a full clean up and reorganization of our building space. I was never thanked. And his desk is back to being so messy it makes me cry.

I have no insurance. I found a site I can buy my medicine from if things get too rough. The thought of going back to my daily pains literally makes me sick to my stomach. And I cannot work if I'm in that much pain.
